July 16, 2024 Your Brain and Diabetes Key points Your brain is sensitive to the amount of glucose (sugar) it receives. Both high and low blood sugar can damage blood vessels in the brain. Help prevent problems by keeping your blood sugar close to target levels. The diabetes-brain connection Your brain is your body's command center. To do all its work, your brain uses sugar in your blood for energy. In fact, the brain is the most energy-demanding organ. It needs half of all the sugar energy in the body to function properly. If your blood sugar levels fall outside your normal range, it can throw your command center off balance. In the same way diabetes can damage nerves in other parts of your body, it can damage nerves in your brain. Diabetes can damage blood vessels in the brain and cause a stroke or memory loss. This can lead to problems with memory and learning, mood shifts, weight gain, and hormonal changes. Over time, it can also lead to other serious problems like Alzheimer's disease. That way you can catch problems early and get them treated right away. Nerve damage About half of all people with diabetes have some kind of nerve damage . Nerves in your feet and legs are most often affected. Nerve damage can cause you to lose feeling in your feet. Some people with nerve damage have numbness, tingling, or pain. Others have no symptoms. Nerve damage can also lower your ability to feel pain, heat, or cold. Pain is the body’s way of telling you something’s wrong so you can take care of yourself. If you don’t feel pain in your feet, you may not notice a cut, blister, sore, or other problem. Small problems can become serious if they aren’t treated early. Could you have nerve damage? May 15, 2024 Your Immune System and Diabetes Key points Having diabetes increases your chances of getting sick, staying sick longer, or getting severely sick. That's because diabetes makes it harder to fight off infectious diseases, illnesses caused by germs. Find out how you can boost your immune system to stay healthy with diabetes. How your immune system works Your immune system recognizes and fights off germs that can make you sick. Many people think of the immune system as protection inside the body. But your first line of defense is your skin, which keeps unwanted germs out. The second layer of your immune system is a type of white blood cells circulating throughout your body known as lymphocytes. These white blood cells are on the lookout for threats that could make you sick, like bacteria, viruses, toxins, or fungi. Once your immune system recognizes these germs, it fights them off, often without you even noticing. Your immune system also helps you build up immunity, or protection, against some viruses. pages.text: Your Neighborhood Could Influence Your Dementia Risk | National Geographic Premium HEALTH Your Neighborhood Could Influence Your Dementia Risk A new study found that dementia-related deaths were highest in certain types of neighborhoods, and the most at-risk might surprise you. Where you live can shape your brain health by influencing your access to medical care, outdoor spaces, and social connection. James Leynse, Getty Images By Katie Wright Published September 16, 2026 A secluded cottage in the quiet countryside might seem better for your brain than a home in a crowded city. But a new study of dementia mortality across England found a more surprising pattern. Researchers at Cambridge University examined data from nearly 41 million individuals in England from 2011 to 2023. Dementia-related deaths were highest not in the most densely populated cities or the most rural areas, but in the suburbs and other mid-density neighborhoods. The researchers calculated that improving access to services and the quality of outdoor spaces in the most disadvantaged communities could prevent up to 10.5 percent of dementia deaths. The findings highlight how our understanding of neurodegenerative disease has evolved. For decades, the search for the causes of dementia focused largely on the brain and body. Now, researchers are increasingly looking outward, examining how the places where people live—and the conditions they encounter there—can shape brain health. pages.text: YouthBuild | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content YouthBuild More in This Section Close About Youth Services WIOA Youth Formula Program Reentry Employment Opportunities Workforce Pathways for Youth YouthBuild GetMyFuture Job Corps Apprenticeship YouthBuild is a community-based pre-apprenticeship program that provides job training and educational services for opportunity youth ages 16-24 who left school without a secondary diploma. Participants learn vocational skills in construction, as well as in other in-demand industries that include healthcare, information technology, and hospitality. Participants also provide community service through the required construction or rehabilitation of affordable housing for low-income or homeless families in their own neighborhoods. Participants split their time between the vocational training work site and the classroom, where they earn their high school diploma or equivalency, learn to be community leaders, and prepare for postsecondary training opportunities, including college, apprenticeships, and employment. Supportive services address barriers throughout participation and the 12-month follow-up period, and may include transportation assistance, childcare, healthcare referrals, and the provision of work attire and personal protective equipment. Administered by the Office of Workforce Investment's Division of Youth Services, YouthBuild serves more than 5,000 youth in approximately 200 YouthBuild programs in more than 40 states. European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations. The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war. But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. pages.text: zipimport — Import modules from Zip archives — Python 3.16.0a2 documentation Navigation index modules | next | previous | Python » 3.16.0a2 documentation » The Python standard library » Importing Modules » zipimport — Import modules from Zip archives | Theme Auto Light Dark | zipimport — Import modules from Zip archives ¶ Source code: Lib/zipimport.py This module adds the ability to import Python modules ( *.py , *.pyc ) and packages from ZIP-format archives. It is usually not needed to use the zipimport module explicitly; it is automatically used by the built-in import mechanism for sys.path items that are paths to ZIP archives. Typically, sys.path is a list of directory names as strings. This module also allows an item of sys.path to be a string naming a ZIP file archive. The ZIP archive can contain a subdirectory structure to support package imports, and a path within the archive can be specified to only import from a subdirectory. For example, the path example.zip/lib/ would only import from the lib/ subdirectory within the archive. Any files may be present in the ZIP archive, but importers are only invoked for .py and .pyc files. ZIP import of dynamic modules ( .pyd , .so ) is disallowed. Note that if an archive only contains .py files, Python will not attempt to modify the archive by adding the corresponding .pyc file, meaning that if a ZIP archive doesn’t contain .pyc files, importing may be rather slow. The work was created in New York in the 1990s, during the early days of the ongoing global AIDS crisis, before any life-saving treatments were available. This was an era marked by tragic loss and the stigmatization of queer people and people of color, along with sex workers and drug users. In this climate of discrimination and neglect, people were dying daily, their bodies treated by the US government and healthcare industries as disposable. After the deaths of several close friends, including fellow artist David Wojnarowicz, Leonard began to sew these fruit pieces. Out of that process, over a period of six years, “Strange Fruit” emerged. The area is tucked between the gray limestone La Madre Mountains to the north, the red sandstone Calico Hills to the west, and a desert ridge to the south. The Calico Basin area is fed year round by water from three permanent springs: Red Spring, Calico Spring, and Ash Spring. The water from these springs support large cottonwood trees, ash trees, scrub live oak, honey mesquite, and saltgrass meadows. Red Spring flows from a shallow tunnel in the rocks along the Red Spring Boardwalk trail, feeding a beautiful marshy grassland and attracting a variety of wildlife. The Red Spring Picnic Area contains picnic tables, metal barbeque grills, trash cans, and restrooms adjacent to the parking area. The area is a good place to see native peoples use of the area including petroglyphs. pages.text: Zora Neale Hurston's 'Barracoon' Tells the Story of the Slave Trade's Last Survivor Skip to main content Zora Neale Hurston Barbara Hurston Lewis, Faye Hurston & Lois Gaston Sitting on his porch in 1928, under the Alabama sun, snacking on peaches, Cudjo Lewis (born Oluale Kossola) recounted to his guest his life story: how he came from a place in West Africa, then traversed the Middle Passage in cruel and inhumane conditions on the famed Clotilda ship, and saw the founding of the freedman community of Africatown after five years of enslavement. After two months of listening to Kossola’s tales, his interlocutor asked to take his picture. Donning his best suit, but slipping off his shoes, Kossola told her, “I want to look lak I in Affica, cause dat where I want to be.” His listener, companion and scribe was Zora Neale Hurston, the celebrated Harlem Renaissance author of Their Eyes Were Watching God. She poured his story, told mostly in his voice and dialect, into Barracoon: The Story of the Last “Black Cargo.” After eight decades, the manuscript is finally being published next week. (The title comes from the Spanish word for an enclosure where slaves were kept before the Middle Passage journey.) Known mostly as a novelist, Hurston also had a career as an anthropologist. She studied under the well-known Franz Boas , who helped establish Columbia University’s anthropology department, in the 1890s, and she conducted fieldwork on voodoo in Haiti and Jamaica and folktales in the American South . pages.text: Zora Neale Hurston’s Study of the Last Known U.S. Slave to Be Published in 2018 Skip to main content Carl Van Vechten Photographs collection at the Library of Congress In 1931, the iconic author Zora Neale Hurston finished writing her almost 120-page book on 95-year-old Cudjo Lewis, the last-known survivor of the Atlantic slave trade. Nearly a century later, Hurston’s study of Lewis has been acquired by HarperCollins, as David Canfield of Entertainment Weekly reports. It is due to be published in May of 2018. Barracoon: The Story of the Last "Black Cargo" recounts Lewis’ long and often harrowing life, from the raid that led to his capture and enslavement, to the vital role he played in founding a town for freed slaves in Alabama. Hurston worked as an anthropologist before publishing seminal works of fiction—most notably Their Eyes Were Watching God —and her work on Lewis relied on years of in-depth interviews and research. She first met Lewis in 1927, according to HarperCollins , and that year published the essay " Cudjo’s Own Story of the Last African Slaver .” The following year, she created a five-minute silent film titled " Kossula: Last of the Takkoi Slaves ." Diouf of the Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, writing for the Encyclopedia of Alabama . In 1860, his town was attacked and Lewis was captured. English Español Français العربية 简中 繁中 Русский Cerrar Existe una gran diferencia entre no ser racista y ser antirracista. Tal vez recuerdes algún momento en el que oíste a alguien decir algo racista o actuar de manera racista. A las personas no racistas no les gusta agitar las aguas. No suelen enfrentarse al adversario. En lugar de decir lo que piensan, normalmente guardan silencio y, si acaso, hablan más tarde sobre lo ocurrido. Las personas antirracistas miran a su alrededor y piensan qué pueden hacer, de qué herramientas disponen o qué pueden decir para dejar claro que la conducta racista es inaceptable. Eso no significa que sean groseras con la gente; lo que hacen es llamar su atención educadamente si escuchan palabras racistas o ven un comportamiento racista. Ser antirracista también implica ver más allá de la conducta individual. Las personas antirracistas se fijan en las causas originarias del racismo sistémico en el poder, las políticas, las instituciones y los casos, y analizan cómo éstas producen o sostienen las jerarquías y desigualdades raciales. pages.text: À propos de IETF - Internet Society À propos de l’Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) Le groupe de travail sur l’ingénierie Internet, soit l’Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) développe des standards ouverts par le biais de processus ouverts avec un objectif précis d’améliorer le fonctionnement d’Internet. L’IETF qui est composé d’une grande communauté internationale de concepteurs, d’opérateurs, de fournisseurs, et de chercheurs, se focalise sur l’évolution de l’architecture Internet, et le bon fonctionnement d’Internet. En savoir plus sur IETF L’Internet Society et l’IETF L’IETF et l’Internet Society sont alignés depuis longtemps sur leur vision en matière de la défense des processus multipartites, et des normes ouvertes. Depuis 1992, nous soutenons l’IETF en servant de siège organisationnel à l’IETF LLC qui est le cadre administratif du travail de l’IETF, et à travers de financements annuels. Nous contribuons au processus de normalisation de l’IETF en nommant le président du comité de nomination de l’IETF, à travers diverses activités telles que le programme des décideurs, et en encourageant d’autres personnes à soutenir le déploiement des normes de l’IETF. Ce dernier joue pour sa part un rôle dans la gouvernance de l’Internet Society en désignant un ensemble d’administrateurs au sein de notre conseil d’administration. Lire plus à propos de nos relations sous le RFC 8712. Vous pouvez également lire l’histoire de la relation telle que présentée par Vint Cerf dès juillet 1995.

pages.text: À propos de la Fondation Internet Society - Internet Society Fondation Internet Society Au fil des ans, l’Internet Society a soutenu le travail inspirant de personnes qui croient en la puissance de l’Internet. Le lancement de la Fondation Internet Society a été une étape importante pour notre organisation et pour notre action en faveur d’un Internet plus étendu et plus performant pour tous. Elle reflète la prochaine étape de nos programmes de bourses et ouvre de nouvelles opportunités en faveur d’initiatives étroitement liées à notre mission. En tant que principale source pour tous les programmes de bourses , la Fondation Internet Society propose des financements destinés à notre communauté et étend sa portée à de nouveaux domaines susceptibles d’avoir un impact positif grâce à la philanthropie. Organisation créée pour venir en soutien à l’Internet Society, la Fondation Internet Society a continué à évoluer, assumant récemment un rôle plus important dans le soutien et la promotion du travail effectué par l’Internet Society. Contrairement au réseau téléphonique, qui pendant des années dans la plupart des pays était géré par une seule entreprise, Internet se compose de dizaines de milliers de réseaux interconnectés gérés mondialement par les fournisseurs de services, des entreprises individuelles, des universités, des gouvernements et d’autres entités. Les standards ouverts permettent à ce réseau de réseaux de communiquer. Cela permet à quiconque de créer du contenu, d’offrir des services et de vendre des produits sans avoir à demander la permission d’une autorité centrale. Savoir plus Qui le fait fonctionner ? L’écosystème Internet est composé de nombreuses organisations et communautés qui aident Internet à marcher et à évoluer. Le développement rapide et continu et l’adoption des technologies d’Internet peuvent être attribués à la participation d’un large éventail de personnes et d’organisations; des processus ouverts, transparents et collaboratifs; ainsi que de l’utilisation de produits et d’infrastructures avec une propriété et un contrôle dispersés. pages.description: Une communauté mondiale de membres, de groupes d’intérêts spéciaux et de plus de 120 chapitres qui s’efforcent de réduire la fracture numérique et de rétablir la confiance en Internet.
pages.text: À propos de l’Internet Society - Internet Society Internet est pour tout le monde. Cette vision détermine tout ce que nous faisons. Internet est pour tout le monde. Cette vision détermine tout ce que nous faisons. Nous sommes une organisation mondiale à but non lucratif, portée par sa communauté. En collaboration avec notre Fondation , nous apportons une expertise technique et en matière de politiques publiques, des infrastructures, des financements et des formations aux compétences – autant de piliers essentiels d’un Internet accessible, fiable et sécurisé. Fidèles aux origines d’Internet, nous sommes profondément attachés à la préservation des fondations sur lesquelles il a été bâti et au développement de tout son potentiel. Découvrez notre histoire . Notre travail Notre travail Internet est une force transformatrice. Mais tout le monde n’en bénéficie pas de la même manière. 2,2 milliards de personnes n’ont toujours pas accès à Internet. Et, de plus en plus, notre sécurité en ligne est mise en péril par le manque de confiance quant au contrôle de nos informations personnelles. Les enjeux n’ont jamais été aussi importants. Vous pensez que nous partageons notre humanité, ainsi que la responsabilité de ce qui se passe dans le monde, qu’importe ce que disent les personnalités politiques ? Si c’est le cas, alors vous êtes l’un·e des nôtres. Notre croyance inébranlable dans le pouvoir citoyen entraîne un changement concret qui s’étend aux quatre coins du monde. Grâce aux années de soutien de sympathisant·e·s engagé·e·s comme vous, la peine de mort a été abolie dans la plupart des pays, de dangereux logiciels espions utilisés pour cibler des militant·e·s ont été exposés, et des tyrans apparemment intouchables ont été amenés à répondre de leurs crimes. Qu’est-ce qu’Amnesty International ? Amnesty International est un mouvement mondial réunissant plus de 10 millions de personnes qui agissent pour que les droits fondamentaux de chacun et chacune soient respectés. Uni·e·s par notre humanité partagée , nous savons que nous avons tous et toutes en nous le pouvoir de créer un changement positif. Nous sommes financés par des membres et des personnes comme vous . Nous sommes indépendants de toute idéologie politique, de tout intérêt économique et de toute religion. pages.text: Émigré Art Networks in Britain | Tate Britain Join us at Tate Britain for a one-day symposium exploring the influence of émigrés on British art and culture This symposium will draw inspiration from our current archive display Together on this Island: Émigré Art Networks in Britain to present the work of art world figures who migrated to Britain from continental Europe in the mid-20th century, many fleeing Nazism, and to consider their contribution to British culture. Drawing on archival research and case studies of individual figures, the programme will explore how émigrés shaped British artistic, intellectual, and public life, while addressing questions of displacement, identity, and belonging. It will also examine the role of institutions and support organisations in fostering cultural exchange and professional networks. Together on this Island: Émigré Art Networks in Britain will be on display in the Marie-Louise von Motesiczky Archive Gallery, Tate Britain until 20 June 2027. This event is generously funded by the Marie-Louise von Motesiczky Charitable Trust.
